title: The anatomy of a shadow — Image Wiki

rules.rule: Reflected light on the shadow side must always remain darker than the darkest part of the lit side; if it is brighter, it indicates a second light source.
rules.evidence: The working rule: on one object under one source, reflected light inside the shadow stays darker than the darkest part of the lit side. Break it and the object reads as a cut-out with a glow behind it.

rules.rule: If an object has no distinct dark seam where it meets the ground, it likely appears to be floating rather than resting on a surface.
rules.evidence: Where the object meets the ground: a distinct dark seam? No seam means it is floating.
